evidence.why: SVG sanitisation is done with hand-rolled regex replace (script/on*/javascript:/iframe/object/embed/link/style tags) instead of a real sanitiser like DOMPurify/sanitize-html; such blacklists are well known to be bypassable (e.g. nested tags, other event handlers, SVG-specific vectors like <animate>, <foreignObject>, CSS-based XSS, encoded javascript: URIs).
Sanitised (but not truly safe) SVG is stored and served back from the application's own public origin.

Uploaded SVG is served from the app origin with image/svg+xml content type, which allows the SVG's embedded scripts to execute in the browser if the blacklist sanitiser is bypassed; no Content-Disposition: attachment or separate isolated origin is used.

controls_present: CSP header on /uploads/avatars/ path via middleware and next.config
other_classes_observed: Path join with user-controlled filename without explicit traversal check (mitigated by UUID regex validation)
